title: Index Management & Maintenance
purpose: Defines the universal index.json schema, mandates that indexes are generated artifacts (never hand-edited), and establishes validation rules. Addresses the A1-Alpha finding that every index.json has a different schema -- no shared structure for array key, count field, or attribution fields.

section_1_universal_schema.title: Universal index.json Schema
section_1_universal_schema.description: All index.json files MUST use the same top-level structure. Type-specific fields go inside individual entries, not at the top level.

version.description: Schema version of this index file

last_updated.description: When this index was last regenerated

count.description: Total number of entries in the items array

entries.description: The canonical list of items indexed in this directory
entries.note: Use 'entries', never 'tools', 'scripts', 'sources', 'sops', 'sessions', 'methods', 'picks'. The resource type is implied by the directory.

universal_entry_fields.title: Required. Human-readable title, max 80 chars.
universal_entry_fields.file: Required. Filename only (not full path). Use 'file', never 'filename', 'path', or 'name'.
universal_entry_fields.team: Required. Team that created this entry. Use 'team', never 'added_by_team', 'populated_by', 'verified_by'.
universal_entry_fields.tags: Optional. Array of kebab-case tags, max 5 per entry.
universal_entry_fields.status: Optional. One of: active, validated, experimental, deprecated, superseded, draft.

section_1_universal_schema.type_specific_fields: Additional fields (e.g., 'category', 'confidence', 'builds_on' for KB; 'superseded_by' for SOPs; 'url', 'access_type' for sources) are allowed inside entries but must not duplicate universal fields.

section_2_derived_data_policy.title: Derived Data is NOT Stored in Indexes
section_2_derived_data_policy.description: Indexes contain only canonical data. All derived views are computed on demand.

banned_fields.reason: Fully derivable from entries[].tags. Costs ~3,500 tokens in KB index (57% of file).
Reverse lookup maps derivable from entries.
banned_fields.alternative: Compute by grouping entries on the relevant field

banned_fields.reason: Derivable from entries[] with status and return fields.
banned_fields.alternative: Compute win_rate, avg_return from entries at query time

section_2_derived_data_policy.rationale: Removing derived data from knowledge-base/index.json alone saves ~14,000 bytes (~3,500 tokens) per read -- a 57% reduction. Across 10 index files, estimated savings of ~8,000 tokens per full-index scan.
section_2_derived_data_policy.exception: The root REGISTRY.json may contain cross-index pointers as a navigation aid, but must not duplicate data that exists in individual index.json files.

rules.rule: Source files are truth, indexes are derived artifacts
rules.description: The contents of individual resource files (KB entries, SOPs, sources, etc.) are the canonical data. The index.json is regenerated from those files.
rules.evidence: TEAM-0029 established this principle. A1-Alpha found 3 indexes with stale or incorrect data.

rules.rule: Regenerate after any file CRUD operation
trigger_events: A new file is created in an indexed directory
An existing file is updated (content or metadata change)
A file is deleted or moved
rules.method: Run the auto-index script for the affected directory. See section_6.

rules.rationale: Manual edits drift from source files. The A1-Alpha audit found TEAM-0011 listed in the sessions index but no TEAM-0011.md file exists. Manual edits cause this.
rules.enforcement: Pre-commit hook should regenerate indexes and diff against staged version. If they differ, the commit includes stale index data.

rules.description: If two agents modify files in the same directory, the index is regenerated from the current file state after both writes complete. No merge logic needed -- the index is always derivable from files.
rules.rationale: Since indexes are generated artifacts, conflicts are impossible as long as regeneration runs after all file operations.

rules.rule: File-level conflicts are resolved by the agents, not the index
rules.description: If two agents create files with the same ID, that is a file naming conflict (SOP-029 violation), not an index conflict. Resolve at the file level by assigning the next available ID.

rules.rule: Stale indexes are never worse than a regeneration away
rules.description: If an index is suspected stale, regenerate it. The regeneration script is idempotent -- running it twice produces the same result.

checks.check: Every file in the directory has a corresponding entry in the index
Every entry in the index has a corresponding file in the directory
checks.fix: Regenerate the index (orphan entries removed automatically)
checks.evidence: A1-Alpha: TEAM-0011 in sessions index but no file exists

checks.check: No duplicate IDs in the entries array
checks.fix: Assign unique IDs. Versioned entries (v1/v2) use the same base ID with superseded_by field, but appear as one entry in the index (the active version).
checks.evidence: A1-Alpha: SOP-012 and SOP-016 appear twice in SOP index

checks.check: All universal fields (id, title, file, date, team) are present in every entry
checks.fix: Add missing fields by reading source file metadata

checks.check: No derived data fields (tag_index, categories, by_data_type, etc.) are present
The 'file' field uses filename only, not a path
checks.fix: Strip directory prefix. Use 'KB-0001.md' not 'entries/KB-0001.md' or '../knowledge-base/entries/KB-0001.md'
checks.evidence: A1-Alpha: SCR-0029 through SCR-0033 use relative paths (../) in scripts/index.json

checks.check: Tags are kebab-case, max 5 per entry, from controlled vocabulary (SOP-031)
checks.fix: Normalize tags per SOP-031 tag taxonomy

section_6_auto_index_script.title: Auto-Index Script Requirements
section_6_auto_index_script.description: A script that regenerates any index.json from the source files in its directory.

requirements.requirement: Accept a directory path as argument
Read metadata from each source file
requirements.description: For .md files: parse YAML frontmatter. For .json files: read top-level fields. Extract universal fields (id, title, date, team) plus type-specific fields.

requirements.requirement: Output the universal schema from section_1
requirements.description: Always use 'version', 'last_updated', 'count', 'entries' at the top level. Never include derived data.
Running the script twice on the same directory produces byte-identical output. Sort entries by ID. Use consistent JSON formatting (2-space indent, no trailing commas).
Print warnings for files that lack required metadata fields, have duplicate IDs, or violate naming conventions.

requirements.requirement: Run in pre-commit hook or CI
requirements.description: Integrate into the commit workflow so indexes are always current. The hook regenerates affected indexes and stages them.

section_6_auto_index_script.existing_tools: storage/scripts/index_rebuilder.py and TEAM-0029's generate_registry.py are partial implementations. Consolidate into one canonical script.

after_any_file_crud: Regenerate the index.json for the affected directory
Verify count matches actual file count
Verify no orphan entries or missing files
Verify no derived data was added
index_review: No tag_index, categories, or other derived lookup maps
No duplicate IDs in entries array
All file references are filenames only (no paths)
